Orc fortress

Setting

Urk-Tar’s fortress is the centre of Kir’s dealings with the orcs. The chief and shaman connect his arrival with memories of Zak, while ritual obligations, a kidnapped wife and conflict with human settlers make the stronghold a place of competing demands. [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]

Urk-Tar and the destroyed expedition

On Gipath, Chief Urk-Tar says his warriors destroyed the Khadaganian expedition. He remembers how Zak’s defeat of a supposed Demon showed that armoured outsiders could be killed, and hopes Kir will become a Chosen for his own tribe. Kel proposes a false report with unpromising stone samples to prevent another imperial expedition from being sent. The shaman Tynachey distrusts strangers but makes Kir a ritual axe after he supplies suitable stone, and makes beads for Kel. Their welcome depends on helping the tribe, and Kir soon rescues the chief from a harpy and his wife from goblins. [2, 3, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 4, 13]

The Shell and the war with the settlers

Urk-Tar explains that humans have driven orcs out of the Foothills and are advancing into the Middle Mountains. Kir removes the Shell whose presence restrains the lizards, initially refusing to fight humans himself. When Tynachey describes the killing of the tribe’s inhabitants, Kel argues for helping their hosts recover the settlement, and Kir agrees. The Hermit Lizard then offers news of the former Chosen in exchange for placing the Shell by the Remote Mountains’ lake. Restoring it also frees hunters held by lizards. The Hermit directs Kir toward the Great Magician by a route different from Zak’s old tunnel approach. [5, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18]
